description: Durably retain Workflow turn events and follow-up user input on the originating runner, retry them in AgentSession order across network failure and runner restart, and keep Server delivery independent of runtime execution.

tasks.title: Deliver AgentSession runtime events durably
tasks.description: Replace the terminal-only fallback and direct Workflow/follow-up uploads with one host-owned `AgentSessionRuntimeEventOutbox`, including durable storage, policy-aware acknowledgement, per-Session FIFO delivery, autonomous health recovery, and idempotent legacy import. Atomically switch Workflow input/activity/close and Workflow/generic follow-up input/outcome producers to the shared outbox so no deliverable revision contains competing queues.
acceptanceCriteria: The shared outbox durably records one-event entries containing a local record ID, binding-free Workflow or generic Session target, original `runtimeSessionId`, optional work metadata, payload, acknowledgement policy, and stable sequence position before starting network delivery; the snapshot uses atomic replacement and owner-only permissions under `.mohist/runner-state/runtime-events.json`.

The real snapshot/import store depends on an injected `RuntimeEventOutboxFileSystem`; tests run that store against a recording in-memory implementation and verify serialization, owner-only write options, temporary-write/rename ordering, restart reload, and failure boundaries without instantiating the Node filesystem adapter or touching a temporary directory.

Workflow input/activity/close and follow-up input use `matching-receipt`: each request sends one queue head and removes it only when `AgentSessionRuntimeEventReceipt[]` contains the submitted type; timeout, transport failure, non-2xx, malformed or empty response, and a receipt without that type retain the head for retry.

Operation-correlated follow-up completed/failed outcomes use `successful-response`: timeout, transport failure, non-2xx, or malformed response retains the record, while any valid 2xx receipt array including `[]` settles it; tests prove both consumed-operation replay and stale-binding empty responses advance the queue without claiming the terminal fact was persisted.

`ServerConnection.agentSessionRuntimeEvents` returns and validates the receipt array already produced by the generic Server route, while the Workflow method retains the same contract; no Server endpoint, DTO, event ID, deduplication/idempotency behavior, persisted model, or external dependency changes.

The outbox preserves FIFO order by canonical logical Session target, allows at most one in-flight head per Session, prevents input/activity/close overtaking across reused turns, and drains other Session queues with bounded concurrency when one head remains unaccepted; stale matching-receipt records remain on their original binding and are never retargeted.

`enqueueBeforeExecution` rolls back an input that fails local persistence and rejects without making it network-deliverable; `enqueueProducedFact` retains an already-produced activity/terminal fact in memory on snapshot failure, marks the outbox unhealthy, and exposes a settled rejection to its producer.

A post-start snapshot failure autonomously retries an atomic snapshot of every retained in-memory record under fake time without requiring another enqueue, work claim, follow-up, or network event; `ready()` becomes true only after successful rename, then pending delivery and execution admission resume.

An unreadable or invalid startup snapshot is never replaced with empty state: autonomous timer plus startup/automatic-reconnect/forced-reconnect triggers retry load idempotently, and health becomes ready only after the existing snapshot is successfully recovered.

Runner startup loads the outbox before accepting commands or claiming work, kicks network drain without awaiting completion, and stop cancels network/local retry timers and HTTP attempts without deleting durable records.

Focused RunnerHost specs prove initial and later outbox unhealthiness prevents polling/claiming even when OpenCode is ready, a full-state recovery succeeds without new work, restored health resumes claims, and already-running work preserves its original result.

`WorkflowAgentSessionReporter` performs no direct HTTP: it awaits durable input enqueue before prompt execution, immediately registers ordered produced-fact promises for normalized live/reconciled events, records one logical completed/failed close, and waits for every local promise to settle without awaiting Server acceptance.

Workflow integration coverage proves rejected input persistence returns explicit execution-unavailable and never calls `OpenCodeRuntime.runTurn` or later delivers the input; rejected activity/close writes after multiple synchronous observer callbacks remain tracked and observable, make the outbox unhealthy, and cannot replace either a successful or failed runtime result.

Focused Workflow specs cover transient and empty-receipt recovery, input/activity/close order, final-response reconciliation, back-to-back turn boundaries, completed/failed terminal convergence, stale-binding retention for matching-receipt events, cross-session progress, non-blocking Server delivery, and restart/reconnect recovery after completed local enqueue.

The follow-up handler awaits durable input enqueue before invoking `runtime.followup`; local failure returns `unavailable` with no invocation, while later Server upload failure/retry never rejects an accepted invocation or invokes the prompt more than once.

Follow-up input and operation-correlated outcomes enter the same Session FIFO in order; dual delivery failure retains both facts, and successful-response terminal acknowledgement preserves the existing operation-fenced behavior without imposing matching-receipt semantics.

RunnerSignalR follow-up specs prove initial/later outbox unhealthiness returns `unavailable` before runtime invocation, autonomous full-state recovery without a new command restores acceptance, and pending network delivery remains active while new commands are gated.

Each valid version-1 `.mohist/runner-state/followup-failures.json` entry imports as an equivalent `successful-response` terminal record with deterministic ID `legacy-followup-terminal:{operationId}`; recorded failures before snapshot write, rename, and legacy marker reconstruct to one record per operation with no lost fact.

`FollowupFailureOutbox`, direct/fire-and-forget Workflow and follow-up event uploads, and their obsolete real-filesystem tests are removed in the same task that activates the shared outbox; no committed deliverable runs both outboxes.

Outbox tests cover coalesced persistence, both acknowledgement policies, ambiguous responses, timeout/retry, concurrent kick idempotency, per-Session ordering, cross-Session isolation, stop/restart, autonomous health recovery, startup load recovery, and migration using recording I/O and fake timers only.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/runner` and `npm test -w packages/runner` pass and leave no Git-visible generated changes.
tasks.output: One shared AgentSession runtime-event outbox and recording-tested snapshot/import store, atomic Workflow/follow-up producer switchover, legacy terminal migration, host and SignalR health gates, and focused runner recovery coverage.
tasks.notes: Implement design decisions D1-D7 as one atomic vertical slice. Do not ship a revision with both outboxes active, send local IDs to the Server, require matching receipts for operation-fenced follow-up terminals, infer persistence from their empty response, retarget stale matching-receipt records, await Server delivery from runtime execution, claim recovery before local commit, or use real filesystem/wall-clock dependencies in tests. The one-node task graph is acyclic.
